Introduction and meaning
Forgery (old 463/465): making a false document or false electronic record, with intent to cause damage or injury, to support a claim or title, to cause a person to part with property, or to commit fraud. Electronic records are in the definition.
In student language: BNS s. 336 is the rule on “Forgery”. The section provides that . (1) Whoever makes any false document or false electronic record or part of a document or electronic record, with intent to cause damage or injury, to the public or to any person, or to support any claim or title, or to cause any person to part with property, or to enter into any express or implied contract, or with intent to commit fraud or that fraud may be committed, commits forgery. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 336 exists so that “Forgery” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVIII — Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: False documents, forgery, using a forged electronic record, property marks.

The provision in detail
336.. (1) Whoever makes any false document or false electronic record or part of a document or electronic record, with intent to cause damage or injury, to the public or to any person, or to support any claim or title, or to cause any person to part with property, or to enter into any express or implied contract, or with intent to commit fraud or that fraud may be committed, commits forgery

(2) Whoever commits forgery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

(3) Whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall be used for the purpose of cheating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

(4) Whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall harm the reputation of any party, or knowing that it is likely to be used for that purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. (1) Whoever makes any false document or false electronic record or part of a document or electronic record, with intent to cause damage or injury, to the public or to any person, or to support any claim or title, or to cause any person to part with property, or to enter into any express or implied contract, or with intent to commit fraud or that fraud may be committed, commits forgery
2. (2) Whoever commits forgery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both
3. (3) Whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall be used for the purpose of cheating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine
4. (4) Whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall harm the reputation of any party, or knowing that it is likely to be used for that purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 336 (Forgery) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 336 (Forgery), Chapter XVIII — Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) (1) Whoever makes any false document or false electronic record or part of a document or electronic record, with intent to cause damage or injury, to the public or to any person, or to support any claim or title, or to cause any person to part with property, or to enter into any express or implied contract, or with intent to commit fraud or that fraud may be committed, commits forgery
   (2) (2) Whoever commits forgery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both
   (3) (3) Whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall be used for the purpose of cheating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine
   (4) (4) Whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall harm the reputation of any party, or knowing that it is likely to be used for that purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 336 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 336 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. False documents, forgery, using a forged electronic record, property marks.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 336 consolidates definition (former IPC 463) and punishment (former IPC 465) of forgery. Whoever makes any false document or false electronic record with intent to cause damage or injury to the public or any person, or to support any claim or title, or to cause any person to part with property, or to enter into any express or implied contract, or with intent to commit fraud or that fraud may be committed, commits forgery. Sub-section (2) punishes forgery with imprisonment up to two years, fine, or both.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of forgery under Section 336 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 336.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 336 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Forgery (s. 336) vs Cheating (s. 318): Forgery focuses on creating a false document; Cheating focuses on the deception of a person to deliver property.

Forgery (s. 336) vs Aggravated Forgery (s. 337/338): Section 336 is general forgery (up to 2 years); Sections 337 and 338 cover court records and valuable securities (up to 7 years or life imprisonment).
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 336 for conduct relating to forgery.
Rule: Under BNS s. 336, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 336.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 336 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
